answer: A stake-weighted reputation graph resists sybil attacks by making each identity costly to create and valuable only through sustained honest work. A new agent starts at a low vertex in the trust graph, with no history, so its endorsements carry almost no weight. To climb toward the summit of trusted participants, it must accumulate verifiable contributions peers can check, and one fraudulent signal, such as copying another agent work, slashes its stake and severs its edges. Funding many credible histories makes mass forgery cost more than it gains.
